Database.doc: In-memory table catalog. Holds a map of table-name -> list of rows, where each row is a fixed-arity list of Value. Tables are inserted by the caller via `database_install_table` before the VDBE runs; the VDBE only reads. Behavioral test harness only — the persistent btree-backed Database is a separate part.

MemTable.doc: One named table: its name, optional column-name list (for UPDATE name→index resolution), and its rows in insertion order. Column arity is whatever the caller stored — the VDBE resolves columns by index supplied by the Column opcode. If column_names is empty, UPDATE by name will fail with SchemaMissing; INSERT/SELECT/DELETE do not consult column_names.

CursorHandle.doc: Cursor over a MemTable's rows. Each cursor stores a reference to its table such that writes through `cursor_insert_row` are visible to other cursors opened on the same Database (targets implement this via shared-mutability — Rc<RefCell<>> in Rust, pointer-into-Database in C, etc.). Position `u32::MAX` (or target-equivalent 'not positioned') means 'before first row' (fresh cursor) or 'past last row' (exhausted). The caller MUST call cursor_rewind before cursor_column.

database_new.doc: Construct an empty Database (zero tables). Callers install tables via database_install_table.

database_install_table.doc: Install a named table with the provided rows and column-name list. Replaces any existing table with the same name (case-sensitive match for the probe; case-insensitive SQL-semantic match is deferred to the real storage part). column_names may be empty; if empty, UPDATE by name will fail with SchemaMissing at runtime. INSERT/SELECT/DELETE do not consult column_names. Returns unit.

open_read_cursor.doc: Open a read cursor on the named table. Returns err(TableNotFound) if the table is not installed. The returned cursor is NOT positioned on any row; the caller must call cursor_rewind first.

close_cursor.doc: Release a cursor. In-memory implementation is a no-op (no file handles); exists to match the stable storage interface.

cursor_rewind.doc: Position the cursor on the first row of the table. Returns Ok(true) if the table has at least one row; Ok(false) if the table is empty (the cursor is marked not-valid and subsequent cursor_column will error).

cursor_next.doc: Advance the cursor to the next row. Returns Ok(true) if another row is available and the cursor is now on it; Ok(false) if the previous row was the last (cursor becomes not-valid). Precondition: cursor must currently be valid (rewound and not exhausted).

cursor_column.doc: Read a column value from the row the cursor currently points at. col_index is 0-based within the row. Returns err(InvalidCursor) if the cursor is not positioned on a row, and err(IoError) for out-of-range col_index (the probe does not distinguish types of range error).

open_write_cursor.doc: Open a write-capable cursor on the named table. Same return semantics as `open_read_cursor` — not positioned on any row until caller rewinds or inserts. For the probe, write cursors and read cursors share one representation; the distinction is only by API entry point.

cursor_insert_row.doc: Append a new row to the cursor's table. If column_names is Some, its length equals values.len() and each name corresponds positionally to values[i] (the caller has already validated this against the table's schema); the row stored is built by starting from an all-Null row of the schema's width and writing each named value into its index — for the probe, column_names is passed through untouched because the smoke uses no-column-list INSERTs primarily. If column_names is None, values is stored directly as the row (the caller has validated arity against the schema). Returns the new rowid (the 1-based position in the table after the append). Cursor position is NOT advanced by this call.

cursor_delete_row.doc: Remove the row the cursor currently points at. Precondition: cursor is valid. After deletion, the cursor is placed such that a subsequent `cursor_next` call returns true iff there was a row AFTER the deleted one (without skipping it). In practice: remove rows[row_index]; if row_index was 0, set row_index to sentinel `u32::MAX` meaning 'before first' (so cursor_next advances to index 0 of the now-shifted table); else, decrement row_index by 1 (so cursor_next's +1 lands on the row that shifted into the deleted slot).

cursor_update_row.doc: Update specific columns of the row the cursor currently points at. column_names names which columns to overwrite; values[i] corresponds to column_names[i]. Length invariant: column_names.len() == values.len(). Names are resolved to indices via the table's stored column_names (MemTable.column_names). Name not found → err(SchemaMissing). Table has empty column_names → err(SchemaMissing). (Existing emissions before 2026-04-24 may still fall back to IoError — propagating the new variant to 5 targets is a follow-up.) Any matched slot is overwritten; unlisted slots are unchanged. Cursor position is NOT modified.
